communicates.content: Well, it was evident from what we have heard that Baskerville has been very closely shadowed by someone since he has been in town. How else could it be known so quickly that it was the Northumberland Hotel which he had chosen?

events.label: Holmes states his earlier argument that shadowing would continue into the second day

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: If they had followed him the first day I argued that they would follow him also the second.

events.label: Holmes tells Watson he twice strolled to the window while Dr. Mortimer was reading his legend

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You may have observed that I twice strolled over to the window while Dr. Mortimer was reading his legend.

events.label: Watson recalls and acknowledges Holmes's actions

communicates.speaker: character_watson
communicates.content: Yes, I remember.

events.label: Holmes says he looked for loiterers in the street but saw none

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I was looking out for loiterers in the street, but I saw none.

events.label: Holmes tells Watson they are dealing with a clever man and describes the situation as deep and involving power and design

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: We are dealing with a clever man, Watson. This matter cuts very deep, and though I have not finally made up my mind whether it is a benevolent or a malevolent agency which is in touch with us, I am conscious always of power and design.

events.label: Holmes follows their friends after they leave in hopes of marking down their invisible attendant
Holmes describes the unknown man's method using a cab to loiter or dash past

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: So wily was he that he had not trusted himself upon foot, but he had availed himself of a cab so that he could loiter behind or dash past them and so escape their notice.

events.label: Holmes states the cab method advantage for following if the friends take a cab

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: His method had the additional advantage that if they were to take a cab he was all ready to follow them.

events.label: Holmes says the cab method has an obvious disadvantage

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It has, however, one obvious disadvantage.

events.label: Watson states the disadvantage is that it puts the man in the power of the cabman

communicates.speaker: character_watson
communicates.content: It puts him in the power of the cabman.

events.label: Holmes agrees with Watson

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Exactly.

events.label: Watson says it is a pity they did not get the cab number

communicates.speaker: character_watson
communicates.content: What a pity we did not get the number!

events.label: Holmes asks if Watson seriously imagines Holmes neglected to get the number

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: My dear Watson, clumsy as I have been, you surely do not seriously imagine that I neglected to get the number?

events.label: Holmes states cab number 2704 is their man

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: 2704 is our man.

events.label: Holmes says the cab number is no use to them for the moment

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: But that is no use to us for the moment.

events.label: Watson says Holmes failed to see how he could have done more

communicates.speaker: character_watson
communicates.content: I fail to see how you could have done more.

events.label: Holmes says he should have turned away instantly upon observing the cab

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: On observing the cab I should have instantly turned and walked in the other direction.

events.label: Holmes proposes alternative follow strategy by hiring a second cab or driving to the Northumberland Hotel and waiting

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I should then at my leisure have hired a second cab and followed the first at a respectful distance, or, better still, have driven to the Northumberland Hotel and waited there.

events.label: Holmes explains that if the unknown followed Baskerville home they would have been able to play his game upon himself

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: When our unknown had followed Baskerville home we should have had the opportunity of playing his own game upon himself and seeing where he made for.

events.label: Holmes states that they betrayed themselves and lost their man due to an indiscreet eagerness taken advantage of quickly by their opponent

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: As it is, by an indiscreet eagerness, which was taken advantage of with extraordinary quickness and energy by our opponent, we have betrayed ourselves and lost our man.

events.label: Holmes and Watson walk slowly down Regent Street while Dr. Mortimer and his companion vanish ahead
Holmes says there is no object in following Dr. Mortimer and his companion and that the shadow has departed

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: There is no object in our following them. The shadow has departed and will not return.

events.label: Holmes tells Watson they must see further cards they have and play them with decision

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: We must see what further cards we have in our hands and play them with decision.

events.label: Holmes asks whether Watson can swear to the man's face within the cab

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Could you swear to that man’s face within the cab?

events.label: Watson says he could swear only to the beard

communicates.speaker: character_watson
communicates.content: I could swear only to the beard.

events.label: Holmes says he could also swear only to the beard

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: And so could I—from which I gather that in all probability it was a false one.

events.label: Holmes states that a clever man on such an errand has no use for a beard except to conceal features

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: A clever man upon so delicate an errand has no use for a beard save to conceal his features.

events.label: Holmes tells Watson to come in

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Come in here, Watson!

events.label: Holmes turns into a district messenger office where he is warmly greeted by the manager
Holmes addresses Wilson and references saving his good name in an earlier case

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Ah, Wilson, I see you have not forgotten the little case in which I had the good fortune to help you?

events.label: Wilson says he has not forgotten and that Holmes saved his good name and perhaps his life

communicates.speaker: character_wilson
communicates.content: No, sir, indeed I have not. You saved my good name, and perhaps my life.

events.label: Holmes replies that Wilson exaggerates and mentions Wilson had a lad named Cartwright

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: My dear fellow, you exaggerate. I have some recollection, Wilson, that you had among your boys a lad named Cartwright, who showed some ability during the investigation.

events.label: Wilson confirms Cartwright is still with them

communicates.speaker: character_wilson
communicates.content: Yes, sir, he is still with us.

events.label: Holmes thanks Wilson
Holmes asks for change of a five-pound note

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: And I should be glad to have change of this five-pound note.

events.label: A manager summons a fourteen-year-old lad who arrives and gazes with reverence at Holmes
Holmes asks for the Hotel Directory

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Let me have the Hotel Directory,

events.label: Holmes gives Cartwright instructions to visit twenty-three hotels near Charing Cross and start by giving outside porters one shilling

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Now, Cartwright, there are the names of twenty-three hotels here, all in the immediate neighbourhood of Charing Cross. Do you see? You will visit each of these in turn. You will begin in each case by giving the outside porter one shilling.

events.label: Cartwright agrees to the instructions

communicates.speaker: character_cartwright
communicates.content: Yes, sir.

events.label: Holmes instructs Cartwright to ask outside porters for the waste-paper of yesterday and to claim an important telegram has miscarried

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You will tell him that you want to see the waste-paper of yesterday. You will say that an important telegram has miscarried and that you are looking for it. You understand?

events.label: Cartwright confirms he understands

communicates.speaker: character_cartwright
communicates.content: Yes, sir.

events.label: Holmes instructs Cartwright that the true target is the centre page of The Times with holes cut out

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: But what you are really looking for is the centre page of the _Times_ with some holes cut in it with scissors. Here is a copy of the _Times_. It is this page. You could easily recognize it, could you not?

events.label: Cartwright confirms he can recognize the page

communicates.speaker: character_cartwright
communicates.content: Yes, sir.

events.label: Holmes instructs Cartwright to give the outside porter and then the hall porter one shilling and obtain the waste or paper heap

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: In each case the outside porter will send for the hall porter, to whom also you will give a shilling. Here are twenty-three shillings. In the three other cases you will be shown a heap of paper and you will look for this page of the _Times_ among it.

events.label: Holmes instructs Cartwright that in many cases the waste will be burned or removed and that there are extra shillings for emergencies and a wire report deadline

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You will then learn in possibly twenty cases out of the twenty-three that the waste of the day before has been burned or removed. In the three other cases you will be shown a heap of paper and you will look for this page of the _Times_ among it. The odds are enormously against your finding it. There are ten shillings over in case of emergencies. Let me have a report by wire at Baker Street before evening.

events.label: Holmes tells Watson that they will find the identity of the cabman number 2704 by wire and then visit Bond Street picture galleries until due at the hotel

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: And now, Watson, it only remains for us to find out by wire the identity of the cabman, No. 2704, and then we will drop into one of the Bond Street picture galleries and fill in the time until we are due at the hotel.

events.label: Holmes has the Hotel Directory
Holmes is absorbed in pictures of modern Belgian masters for two hours
A clerk tells Watson and Holmes that Sir Henry Baskerville is upstairs expecting them

communicates.speaker: character_hall_porter
communicates.content: “Sir Henry Baskerville is upstairs expecting you.” / “He asked me to show you up at once when you came.”

events.label: Holmes asks to look at the hotel register and the clerk permits it

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: “Have you any objection to my looking at your register?”

events.label: Two names are shown as added after Baskerville’s name in the hotel register
A porter identifies Theophilus Johnson as the coal-owner and not the older grey-headed lawyer with a limp

communicates.speaker: character_hall_porter
communicates.content: “No, sir, this is Mr. Johnson, the coal-owner, a very active gentleman, not older than yourself.” / “he has used this hotel for many years, and he is very well known to us.”

events.label: Holmes and Watson learn that Mrs. Oldmore is an invalid lady whose husband was once mayor of Gloucester

communicates.speaker: character_hall_porter
communicates.content: “She is an invalid lady, sir. Her husband was once mayor of Gloucester. She always comes to us when she is in town.”

events.label: Holmes indicates that people interested in Sir Henry are not settled down in his own hotel

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: “We know now that the people who are so interested in our friend have not settled down in his own hotel... That means that while they are... very anxious to watch him, they are equally anxious that he should not see them. Now, this is a most suggestive fact.”

events.label: Sir Henry Baskerville confronts Holmes and Watson on the stairs holding a missing boot
Sir Henry says he believes hotel people have taken his boots and may cause trouble

communicates.speaker: character_sir_henry_baskerville
communicates.content: “Seems to me they are playing me for a sucker in this hotel... By thunder, if that chap can’t find my missing boot there will be trouble... I can take a joke... but they’ve got a bit over the mark this time.”

events.label: Sir Henry reports that a new brown boot is missing and an old black boot was taken instead

communicates.speaker: character_sir_henry_baskerville
communicates.content: “So it was, sir. And now it’s an old black one.” / “Last night they took one of my brown ones, and today they have sneaked one of the black.”

events.label: A German waiter appears and reports that he can hear no word of the boot

communicates.speaker: character_german_waiter
communicates.content: “No, sir; I have made inquiry all over the hotel, but I can hear no word of it.”

events.label: Sir Henry threatens to see the manager if the boot is not returned before sundown

communicates.speaker: character_sir_henry_baskerville
communicates.content: “Well, either that boot comes back before sundown or I’ll see the manager and tell him that I go right straight out of this hotel.”

events.label: Holmes says it is worth troubling about and asks Sir Henry why it happened
Holmes states that Sir Henry’s case is complex and that threads may guide them to the truth

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: “I just don’t attempt to explain it... It seems the very maddest, queerest thing that ever happened to me.” / “This case of yours is very complex, Sir Henry... But we hold several threads in our hands, and the odds are that one or other of them guides us to the truth.” / “We may waste time in following the wrong one, but sooner or later we must come upon the right.”

events.label: Holmes asks Sir Henry’s intentions and Sir Henry says he will go to Baskerville Hall at the end of the week

communicates.speaker: character_sir_henry_baskerville
communicates.content: “To go to Baskerville Hall.” / “At the end of the week.”

events.label: Holmes questions Dr. Mortimer about being followed from Holmes’s house that morning

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: “You did not know, Dr. Mortimer, that you were followed this morning from my house?”

events.label: Holmes asks Dr. Mortimer about a neighbor on Dartmoor with a black full beard and Dr. Mortimer names Barrymore

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: “Have you among your neighbours or acquaintances on Dartmoor any man with a black, full beard?”

events.label: Holmes instructs sending telegram forms and texts to check whether Barrymore is at Baskerville Hall

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: “Give me a telegraph form. ‘Is all ready for Sir Henry?’ That will do... What is the nearest telegraph-office? Grimpen... Very good, we will send a second wire to the postmaster, Grimpen: ‘Telegram to Mr. Barrymore to be delivered into his own hand. If absent, please return wire to Sir Henry Baskerville, Northumberland Hotel.’”

events.label: Dr. Mortimer describes Barrymore as the son of the deceased old caretaker and says he and his wife are respectable

communicates.speaker: character_james_mortimer
communicates.content: “He is the son of the old caretaker, who is dead... They have looked after the Hall for four generations now... So far as I know, he and his wife are as respectable a couple as any in the county.”

events.label: Holmes asks whether Barrymore profited under Sir Charles’s will and Dr. Mortimer answers that Barrymore and his wife each received five hundred pounds

communicates.speaker: character_james_mortimer
communicates.content: “He and his wife had five hundred pounds each.”

events.label: Dr. Mortimer states residue of Sir Charles’s estate is seven hundred and forty thousand pounds and that the residue went to Sir Henry

communicates.speaker: character_james_mortimer
communicates.content: “The residue all went to Sir Henry.” / “Seven hundred and forty thousand pounds.”

events.label: Holmes and the others discuss who would inherit the estate and Sir Henry says he has not made his will

communicates.speaker: character_sir_henry_baskerville
communicates.content: “No, Mr. Holmes, I have not.”

events.label: Holmes arranges that Watson accompany Sir Henry down to Devonshire

communicates.speaker: character_sir_henry_baskerville
communicates.content: “Well, now, that is real kind of you, Dr. Watson,”... “If you will come down to Baskerville Hall and see me through I’ll never forget it.” / “I will come, with pleasure,” said I.

events.label: Sir Henry retrieves his missing boot from under a cabinet
Mortimer and Baskerville state they searched the room carefully before lunch and the boot was not there then

communicates.speaker: character_james_mortimer
communicates.content: “I searched this room carefully before lunch.”

events.label: A German attendant is sent for but claims to know nothing about the boot’s placement

communicates.speaker: character_german_waiter
communicates.content: “...professed to know nothing of the matter”

events.label: Holmes receives two telegrams, one about Barrymore being at the Hall and one about inability to trace a cut sheet of The Times
Holmes states two threads are gone and they must cast around for another scent

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: “There go two of my threads, Watson... We must cast round for another scent.”

events.label: Holmes states he has wired to get the cabman’s name and address from the Official Registry

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: “I have wired to get his name and address from the Official Registry.”

events.label: A rough-looking fellow enters Holmes’s door and states he came to ask Holmes questions about a fare at 2704

communicates.speaker: character_clayton
communicates.content: “I got a message from the head office that a gent at this address had been inquiring for No. 2704... I came here straight from the Yard to ask you to your face what you had against me.”

events.label: Holmes questions the cabman and the cabman gives his name and address

communicates.speaker: character_clayton
communicates.content: “John Clayton, 3 Turpey Street, the Borough... My cab is out of Shipley’s Yard, near Waterloo Station.”

events.label: Holmes asks the cabman to describe the fare who watched the house at ten o’clock and followed two gentlemen
The cabman says the fare identified himself as a detective and instructed him not to tell anyone

communicates.speaker: character_clayton
communicates.content: “The gentleman told me that he was a detective and that I was to say nothing about him to anyone.” / “Yes, he did.”

events.label: The cabman reports that the detective’s name was Mr. Sherlock Holmes

communicates.speaker: character_clayton
communicates.content: “...was Mr. Sherlock Holmes.”

events.label: Holmes laughs and says it was a touch and tells Watson about the prior interaction

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: “A touch, Watson—an undeniable touch!” / “I feel a foil as quick and supple as my own.” / “He got home upon me very prettily that time.”

events.label: The cabman describes the detective hailing him at Trafalgar Square and making arrangements for following two gentlemen

communicates.speaker: character_clayton
communicates.content: “He hailed me at half-past nine in Trafalgar Square... he said that he was a detective... First we drove down to the Northumberland Hotel and waited... We followed their cab... We pulled up... and waited an hour and a half.”

events.label: John Clayton says he arrived under ten minutes

communicates.speaker: character_clayton
communicates.content: I whipped up the mare and we were there under the ten minutes.

events.label: John Clayton says the cabman threw up the trap and ordered him to drive to Waterloo Station

communicates.speaker: character_clayton
communicates.content: Then my gentleman threw up the trap, and he cried that I should drive right away to Waterloo Station as hard as I could go.

events.label: John Clayton says the gentleman paid two guineas and went into the station

communicates.speaker: character_clayton
communicates.content: Then he paid up his two guineas, like a good one, and away he went into the station.

events.label: John Clayton says the gentleman turned around and told him he had been driving Mr. Sherlock Holmes

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It might interest you to know that you have been driving Mr. Sherlock Holmes.

events.label: John Clayton says that is how he came to know the name

communicates.speaker: character_clayton
communicates.content: That’s how I come to know the name.

events.label: John Clayton says he saw no more of the gentleman after he went into the station

communicates.speaker: character_clayton
communicates.content: Not after he went into the station.

events.label: John Clayton attempts to describe Mr. Sherlock Holmes as a forty-years-old middle-height man with a black square-cut beard and a pale face

communicates.speaker: character_clayton
communicates.content: I’d put him at forty years of age, and he was of a middle height, two or three inches shorter than you, sir. He was dressed like a toff, and he had a black beard, cut square at the end, and a pale face. I don’t know as I could say more than that.

events.label: John Clayton says he cannot say the colour of Mr. Sherlock Holmes's eyes

communicates.speaker: character_clayton
communicates.content: No, I can’t say that.

events.label: John Clayton says he has nothing more he can remember

communicates.speaker: character_clayton
communicates.content: No, sir; nothing.

events.label: Holmes gives John Clayton a half-sovereign and offers another for more information, then ends the encounter

communicates.speaker: character_watson
communicates.content: Well, then, here is your half-sovereign. There’s another one waiting for you if you can bring any more information. Good-night!

events.label: John Clayton departs chuckling and Holmes turns to Watson with a shrug and rueful smile
Holmes says the third thread snaps and they end where they began

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Snap goes our third thread, and we end where we began.

events.label: Holmes states that the opponent knew their number and sent an audacious message by arranging that the driver would be told he had been driving Mr. Sherlock Holmes

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: He knew our number, knew that Sir Henry Baskerville had consulted me, spotted who I was in Regent Street, conjectured that I had got the number of the cab and would lay my hands on the driver, and so sent back this audacious message.

events.label: Holmes says he has been checkmated in London and wishes Watson better luck in Devonshire

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I’ve been checkmated in London. I can only wish you better luck in Devonshire.

events.label: Holmes tells Watson it is an ugly dangerous business and he is less easy in mind about sending him

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: But I’m not easy in my mind about it. About sending you. It’s an ugly business, Watson, an ugly dangerous business, and the more I see of it the less I like it. Yes, my dear fellow, you may laugh, but I give you my word that I shall be very glad to have you back safe and sound in Baker Street once more.

events.label: Holmes gives Watson parting injunctions and advice before they travel to Devonshire

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I will not bias your mind by suggesting theories or suspicions, Watson; I wish you simply to report facts in the fullest possible manner to me, and you can leave me to do the theorizing.

events.label: Watson asks what sort of facts Holmes wants reported

communicates.speaker: character_watson
communicates.content: What sort of facts?

events.label: Holmes instructs Watson to report any facts bearing on the case, especially relations between young Baskerville and his neighbours and particulars concerning the death of Sir Charles

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Anything which may seem to have a bearing however indirect upon the case, and especially the relations between young Baskerville and his neighbours or any fresh particulars concerning the death of Sir Charles.

events.label: Holmes reports that his inquiries have had negative results

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I have made some inquiries myself in the last few days, but the results have, I fear, been negative.

events.label: Holmes states that James Desmond is the next heir and is an elderly amiable gentleman

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: One thing only appears to be certain, and that is that Mr. James Desmond, who is the next heir, is an elderly gentleman of a very amiable disposition, so that this persecution does not arise from him.

events.label: Holmes says they may eliminate James Desmond from their calculations

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I really think that we may eliminate him entirely from our calculations.

events.label: Holmes and Watson discuss who will surround Sir Henry Baskerville on the moor and list multiple suspect groups
Holmes tells Watson to tell Sir Henry Baskerville to keep a revolver near him and never relax precautions

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Most certainly. Keep your revolver near you night and day, and never relax your precautions.

events.label: Dr. Mortimer tells Watson and Holmes there is no news and that they have not been shadowed for two days

communicates.speaker: character_james_mortimer
communicates.content: No, we have no news of any kind; I can swear to one thing, and that is that we have not been shadowed during the last two days. We have never gone out without keeping a sharp watch, and no one could have escaped our notice.

events.label: Mortimer tells the group they were together except yesterday afternoon when he went to the Museum of the College of Surgeons

communicates.speaker: character_james_mortimer
communicates.content: Except yesterday afternoon. I usually give up one day to pure amusement when I come to town, so I spent it at the Museum of the College of Surgeons.

events.label: Baskerville says he looked at the folk in the park and that there was no trouble

communicates.speaker: character_sir_henry_baskerville
communicates.content: And I went to look at the folk in the park; But we had no trouble of any kind.

events.label: Holmes tells Sir Henry Baskerville not to go about alone and warns of misfortune

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I beg, Sir Henry, that you will not go about alone. Some great misfortune will befall you if you do.

events.label: Sir Henry tells Holmes he has not got his other boot

communicates.speaker: character_sir_henry_baskerville
communicates.content: No, sir, it is gone forever.

events.label: Holmes warns Sir Henry to remember a phrase from a legend and avoid the moor during hours of darkness

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Bear in mind, Sir Henry, one of the phrases in that queer old legend which Dr. Mortimer has read to us, and avoid the moor in those hours of darkness when the powers of evil are exalted.

events.label: Holmes is seen standing motionless on the platform as the train begins to depart
The train journey proceeds and Watson and Dr. Mortimer's spaniel are involved in activities during travel
The group descends at a small wayside station, and a wagonette waits outside behind a fence
Two men in dark uniforms with short rifles watch the group as they pass by the gate
A driver salutes Sir Henry Baskerville and the wagonette leaves down the road
Dr. Mortimer asks about the mounted soldier and the driver explains an escaped convict is being sought

communicates.speaker: character_driver
communicates.content: There’s a convict escaped from Princetown, sir. He’s been out three days now, and the warders watch every road and every station, but they’ve had no sight of him yet. The farmers about here don’t like it, sir, and that’s a fact.

events.label: Mortimer and the driver discuss rewards and danger to anyone giving information

communicates.speaker: character_james_mortimer
communicates.content: Well, I understand that they get five pounds if they can give information.

events.label: The driver says the convict would stop at nothing and identifies him as Selden, the Notting Hill murderer

communicates.speaker: character_driver
communicates.content: You see, it isn’t like any ordinary convict. This is a man that would stick at nothing. It is Selden, the Notting Hill murderer.

events.label: The wagonette reaches Baskerville Hall and Sir Henry Baskerville is introduced as its master after a point where the road is named
The party reaches the lodge-gates, passes through the gateway into the avenue, and wheels are hushed amid leaves
A tall man opens the door of the wagonette and a silhouetted woman comes out to help hand down bags

communicates.speaker: character_hall_tall_man
communicates.content: Welcome, Sir Henry! Welcome to Baskerville Hall!

events.label: Dr. Mortimer says he will drive straight home because his wife is expecting him

communicates.speaker: character_james_mortimer
communicates.content: You don’t mind my driving straight home, Sir Henry? My wife is expecting me.

events.label: Mortimer declines dinner and departs, telling Sir Henry to let Barrymore guide him and instructing him to send for Mortimer at any time

communicates.speaker: character_james_mortimer
communicates.content: Surely you will stay and have some dinner? No, I must go. I shall probably find some work awaiting me. I would stay to show you over the house, but Barrymore will be a better guide than I. Good-bye, and never hesitate night or day to send for me if I can be of service.

events.label: Sir Henry and Watson enter the hall and the door closes behind them
Barrymore returns from taking luggage to the rooms and stands in the hall
Barrymore asks if dinner should be served at once and offers hot water while describing the need for a considerable staff under new conditions

clues.significance: Holmes examined the visitor’s stick and used its condition (worn ferrule and knockabout state) as the basis for inferring that the visitor walked a great deal as he traveled.
Holmes used the engraved initials 'C.C.' on the stick as the basis for inferring a hospital connection, suggesting Charing Cross Hospital.
Holmes used the date on the stick (1884) as the basis for inferring that Dr. Mortimer left five years ago from the hospital service.
Holmes used visible marks on the stick (teeth marks associated with the dog) as the basis for identifying the dog as a curly-haired spaniel.
Holmes inferred the date of the manuscript from script usage (the alternative use of the long s and short s).
Mortimer indicated the manuscript's date by stating it was an exact date and showing the '1742' mark associated with the document content.
Holmes inferred from the pasted typography and cut quality that the words were taken from the leading article of yesterday's issue of the Times.
Holmes identified cab number 2704 as the relevant cabman in the case.
Watson found a written message indicating a secret man’s report about Watson’s whereabouts.
Holmes treated Selden’s death as the result of hound pursuit enabled by an article of Sir Henry’s clothing, reasoning from Holmes’s statement that the hound was laid on from Sir Henry’s boot

Holmes inferred that Stapleton's face had been hidden in the portrait by aligning a candle flame with the portrait so that the face 'sprung out of the canvas' and used it as a missing link toward capturing Stapleton.
